7.heading: am 4036, ad 32
refs: A tetrarch, τετραρχης [ G5076 ], from τετρας [ G5069 ], four, and αρχη [ G746 ], government, properly signifies a prince, or ruler over a quarter of any region

and had its origin from Galatia, which was governed by four princes. In the New Testament, however, it denotes a prince, or king, who reigns over the fourth part of a former kingdom. By Herod's will his kingdom was thus divided among his sons: Archelaus had one-half, consisting of Idumea, Judea, and Samaria
Herod Antipas, one-fourth, consisting of Galilee and Perea
and Philip the remaining fourth, consisting of Batanea, Trachonitis, and Auranitis.
